claims.text: As-sintered boride surfaces are chemically active and susceptible to molten-aluminum attack at approximately 660°C.
Rapid laser surface remelting should be applied to the as-sintered boride surface.
Laser surface remelting can enhance the surface characteristics of the proposed boride-based components.
Rapid laser remelting will densify the boride surface and reduce its porosity.
Rapid laser remelting will refine or nanostructure the boride surface layer.
Laser remelting locally melts and rapidly resolidifies the boride surface.
The remelted surface will form an intrinsic, continuous diffusion barrier.
Reduced porosity and discontinuities in the remelted layer will limit molten-aluminum diffusion or infiltration into the substrate.
Limiting aluminum infiltration will reduce molten-aluminum corrosion.
Laser-treated components will exhibit significantly lower weight loss than untreated as-sintered components under identical molten-aluminum exposure.
Laser-treated components will exhibit a reduced depth of aluminum penetration relative to untreated as-sintered components.
Reduced corrosion will extend component lifetime during molten-aluminum exposure.
The improvement should persist during prolonged exposure to molten aluminum at approximately 660°C under typical plating-operation durations.
Excessive laser-induced thermal gradients may generate cracking or residual stresses that compromise corrosion resistance.
Loss of continuity in the remelted layer or operation beyond the refined microstructure's thermal stability may reduce effectiveness.
The magnitude of the corrosion-resistance improvement is uncertain and may vary with laser parameters and component geometry.

A controlled comparison of treated and untreated specimens under identical exposure conditions can falsify the hypothesis if no statistically significant corrosion reduction is observed or if detrimental cracking occurs.
